findings.description: The thirty-seventh-run guard against borrowing the lock holder's MODELINV row keys only on the attempts file: `if [[ -n "$final" && "${_lastrow##*:}" != lock_wait ]]; then _diag=$(_companion_ledger_message ...)`. But `_adv_reap_companion_timed_out` records a companion reaped while in `queue` by writing `lock_wait` to companion.status and copying companion.current to companion.final without appending a `<hop>:lock_wait` row to companion.attempts (the walker was TERM/KILLed and did not write one). The fold then sees `status=lock_wait` yet `_lastrow` is the previous hop's row (or empty when attempts is absent), so the ledger lookup still runs for a hop that never sent a request, over a window (`hop_started_iso`/`started_iso` to `ended_iso`) in which the primary, holding the same shared CLI lock, wrote its own rows for that model.
findings.failure_mode: On the documented host shape (primary and companion both ending on claude-headless, companion queued behind the primary's lock and reaped at bound+30), a failed primary call's provider message is attributed to the companion as `last_error`, and `_companion_failure_class` may classify from that borrowed text instead of the reaper's `lock_wait` status.
findings.suggested_fix: Also skip the ledger lookup when the recorded status is lock_wait: `if [[ -n "$final" && "$status" != lock_wait && "${_lastrow##*:}" != lock_wait ]]`. Alternatively have `_adv_reap_companion_timed_out` append `${final}:lock_wait` to companion.attempts when it writes the lock_wait status, so the attempts record and the status agree.

findings.description: The comment states that a pid forked before the freeze 'carries the token kill_tree took while it was frozen'. The code does the opposite. `_ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS` is first filled by `_adv_pid_tokens` on the unfrozen tree, and the merge loop `[[ " $_ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS" == *" ${_e%%=*}="* ]] || _ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS+="$_e "` keeps the pre-freeze entry for every pid already present, discarding the frozen token from `_kt`. When the pre-freeze `_adv_proc_start` read failed transiently (token ""), that empty token is what `_adv_kill_same` consults five seconds later, so the pid alone decides the KILL even though a valid frozen token was available.
findings.failure_mode: A descendant that exited on TERM and whose pid was reused within the grace period is KILLed by pid alone in exactly the case the frozen-token design was meant to close; low likelihood (requires a failed /proc read plus pid reuse within the grace), but the intended safeguard is not in effect.
findings.suggested_fix: In the merge loop, replace an existing entry whose token is empty with the frozen one from `_kt` (e.g. rebuild `_ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS` from `_kt` first and only then append pre-freeze entries for pids `_kt` lacks), and update the comment to match.

findings.description: Both `_adv_shared_hop_verdict` (`[[ -s result.json && canon == hop ]] && jq empty result.json` → `skip answered_with_it`) and `_fold_companion` (`jq empty < companion.result.json` → `comp_status=succeeded`) treat any syntactically valid JSON as a companion answer. `jq empty` passes for `null`, a number, a string or an array. `_adv_inv5_rewrite` in the same hunk already uses the stricter `jq -e 'type == "object"'`, so the three validators disagree.
findings.failure_mode: A companion.result.json holding `null` (e.g. a walker that captured an empty jq result and wrote it) makes the primary cede its shared last hop to a companion that produced no findings; in the fold, `null` yields a 'succeeded' companion with zero findings and cost 0, while a string or array result fails inside the fold's jq and surfaces only as `fold_failed`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `jq -e 'type == "object" and (.findings // [] | type) == "array"' companion.result.json >/dev/null 2>&1` in both places, matching `_adv_inv5_rewrite`.

findings.description: The companion diagnostic is withheld when the shared redactor exits non-zero, but when `$_redactor` is not executable (`[[ -x "$_redactor" ]]` false, including an `_ADV_REDACTOR_BIN` override pointing at a missing path) the raw line skips the shared redactor entirely and only the sk/xai/gsk/AIza mask runs before `log "Companion voice diagnostic ($final): $last_error"` writes it to stderr. The comment lists the shapes the shared redactor alone covers: URL credentials, AKIA keys, Bearer tokens, PEM material. The envelope value is still allowlisted by `_adv_error_summary`, so exposure is limited to the operator-facing log.
findings.failure_mode: On a checkout or override where lib/log-redactor.sh is absent, a provider error line echoing a Bearer token or a credentialed URL from the companion log or MODELINV row is printed to stderr unredacted.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed consistently: if the redactor is not executable, set `last_error="[diagnostic withheld: no redactor]"` (and log a WARN once) instead of passing the raw line through the narrower mask.
